edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: These exposures act mainly through renal sodium handling, vascular smooth-muscle tone, and neurohormonal blood-pressure regulation. That makes them particularly relevant to Hypertension when salt sensitivity, baseline blood pressure, or medication use already place the system under stress.
edges.summary: In general adult, pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest that potassium tracks with lower risk of hypertension. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
